reply_text:
㊥ ("how far we are from closing any row") Two rows, `InputContext.atEnd` and `Parser.epsilonInfo`, already compile but give different results from Lean, and each looks like one fix away from matching. I've put two Codex agents on closing exactly those two, starting as soon as their current cold runs report. Neither has been tested since A+B merged, so whether one fix is enough is still unconfirmed. Every other row is several stops away, and none of tonight's merges has turned a row correct yet.

㊟ ("just keep going?") Not unchanged. Tonight's work has been moving rows to later stops, and the chart shows that, but the count of correct rows still stands at 20, where it was at 18:22. I'm keeping the stop-by-stop work going, since it has the most rows waiting on it: term[_] C, macro scopes, def result types. But closing these two rows now comes first for two agents, because that's the only work that changes the correct-row count tonight.

㊢ (the two rows)
- **`atEnd`** (codex-19, job `invoke-1791164987180-32448-a37ed671`): the port emits `GE_ge(inst, p, c.endPos)` with three arguments where the function takes four. Lean's term is `decide (p ≥ c.endPos)` with `String.instDecidableLeRaw`, a Prop-to-Bool coercion (`atend-ge.md`). codex-19 already has a branch for that coercion, `psw/prop-bool-coercion`, which was held waiting on exactly this check. Next it merges the current cand-1, then runs the Lean check warm.
- **`epsilonInfo`** (codex-25, job `invoke-1791164990200-32449-ef1d11f5`): it compiled warm at `15c6be52`. Per `wrongresult1.md`, the emitted `ParserInfo` has the wrong values for the two fields Lean leaves at their defaults (`collectTokens`, `collectKinds`, which should be `id`). codex-25 first checks whether its earlier fix for those fields is already in cand-1, then runs the Lean check warm.

🈳 (how far, in time) If either matches warm, cold acceptance is a single run: about 25 to 60 minutes at the current machine load. Then I merge it, and the correct count goes from 20 to 21. If the warm check shows a further mismatch, each agent reports the exact difference from Lean's term before changing anything. Both start only after their current cold runs finish, so the first warm result is probably about an hour away.

previous_reply_acts.text: (progress) Since about 23:00, six compiler fixes have been merged into cand-1, now at `e251cb68`: panic, `EST.Out`, optParam, field notation, null receiver, and term[_] shapes A+B together. Each passed cold acceptance: its target rows got past their stop and the controls matched Lean. No new row has become fully correct yet. What has changed is that rows reach later stops. An integration check of all six merged together has the first control done and matching; the other three are still running.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-4
previous_reply_acts.text:
(what moved)
- **Null receiver** (codex-4): `nodeFn` and `atomicFn` now get past the `null.stackSize`/`null.pos` stop. On the chart, that group fell from 11 to 3, once codex-4's warm re-probes of the other rows were recorded.
- **term[_] A+B** (codex-18 and codex-24): `List.foldlM`, `updateLeading` and `mkUnexpectedError` get past the coercion and `do_lift` stops, then stop at shape C (the ``` ``(…) ``` quotation inside `withAnnotateTerm`). codex-24 starts on C next.
- **Field notation** (codex-29): `crlfToLf` gets past its stop and reaches the `let_mvar` name clash. codex-18's macro-scope fix is aimed at that clash.
- **panic, `EST.Out`, optParam** (codex-25, codex-27, codex-28): each moved one row one stop further on.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-4
previous_reply_acts.text: (the chart) The term[_] bar has gone up, to 50 rows. That's because the null-receiver rows moved onto the term[_] stop, and most term[_] rows haven't been re-probed since A+B merged. The chart will lag until C lands and those rows are re-probed.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-4
previous_reply_acts.text:
(what went wrong)
- **binrel:** codex-18 failed five times in a row the same way, so I paused it. claude-3 then found the real cause: the port has no type for `Ne`, because Lean's `def Ne … := ¬(a = b)` has no written result type. codex-29 is now fixing that in general (`psw/deftype`).
- **Numerals:** codex-19's first fix broke `Array.extract`. Cold acceptance caught it before merging. The rework matches warm and is now in cold acceptance.
- **Macro scopes:** codex-18's first fix passed its own test while the defect was still there. The test exercised only one macro runtime, and production uses two. The rework uses one shared scope supply and a two-runtime test.
- **My mistakes:** I quoted the `nomatch` error without its quote marks, which cost one 12-minute rerun. And one merge conflict needed resolving: I kept codex-28's accepted optParam code over an older version of the same binder logic carried on the A+B branch.

- **Discovery / tooling:** C is next for codex-24. codex-23's term-capture tool for the Lean-trace comparator is still with codex-23.
- **Rob's main:** codex-4 merges cand-1 into the Rob merge branch next, then runs the 20-row cold acceptance. I'll come back to you before anything is pushed to Rob's main.
